selection_rationale: A comprehensive original investigation into how verifiable 2024–2026 civilian preparedness programmes interact with foreign information interference, media amplification, public confidence and critical-infrastructure interdependence; differentiates real risk, warning, attributed campaigns and unsupported collapse claims.
contrary_evidence: Emergency stockpiling and 72-hour household self-sufficiency guidance date to 2024–2025, rather than a single unprecedented November 2026 European crisis announcement.
The 7 November 2026 Brazilian ministry clarification rejects the interpretation of domestic kit guidance as an extraordinary warning of generalized national collapse.
Observed foreign information manipulation campaigns do not establish responsibility for specific food-and-water preparedness headlines without distribution and attribution evidence.
Infrastructure and geopolitical vulnerabilities are material, so dismissing all civil preparedness as propaganda would be equally unfounded.
limitations: No case-specific network forensic attribution for the November 2026 social-media stockpiling narrative; the investigation distinguishes documented general FIMI activity from the untested claim of a coordinated campaign targeting these particular alerts.
EEAS 2025 FIMI incident shares describe a selected observed sample, not the universe of online misinformation or population-level persuasion.
Eurobarometer 2024 household preparedness data are self-reported and cannot be interpreted as audited stocks or current November 2026 rates.
No evidence from the researched official preparedness documents establishes a calendar for imminent Western collapse; absence of such evidence does not rule out future emergencies.
National emergency-kit guidance varies in its water-use definitions, recommendations and geographic contexts.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 8 November 2026, America/Sao_Paulo; official October–November 2026 updates and prior European institutional records included.
producer_checks.research_depth: 18 analytical chapters per locale, 23 numbered references; PT-BR 42,332 characters (~5,637 words), EN 41,014 characters (~5,286 words).
producer_checks.evidence_inventory: 23 matched references per language; European Commission, UK Cabinet Office, NATO, EEAS, Council of the EU, Sweden, Germany's BBK, Brazilian federal civil defense, EU DisinfoLab, peer-reviewed risk psychology, WHO and OECD.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Two auditable matching bar charts in both locales: EEAS attribution shares [29,6,65] and Eurobarometer preparedness categories [47,36,29,20,20,18,16,11]. Both have two comparative tables, a dual-chain flow, a mindmap and a regional exposure map.
producer_checks.translation_check: Identical 18 numbered argument chapters, 23 numbered bibliography entries, numeric chart arrays, comparative table logic and causal/geographic visuals; qualifications concerning attribution and imminent collapse preserved.
producer_checks.factual_cautions: Distinguishes government hazard planning from military intelligence of immediate danger, direct detection of FIMI from attribution of particular panic narratives, and hypothetical supply chain feedbacks from measured shortages.
